title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: up to 100 review sets per case (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the higher limit and the listed control paths and commands are supported, but the page incorrectly says review sets are created only by people. Microsoft documents application-only creation through Graph, so the assurance about human-only actions needs removing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature is included in premium eDiscovery access under Office 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5 or related E5 add-on subscriptions.
claims.quote: If your organization has an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 subscription (or related E5 add-on subscriptions), you can further manage cases and analyze content by using premium eDiscovery features.

claims.where: What's changing: review set definition; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Adding collected mailbox and site content to review sets copies it from its original location.
claims.quote: Adding data to a review set is a long-running process that includes gathering items from the original data sources in Microsoft 365 (for example, from mailboxes and sites), copying them to the Azure Storage location

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Review set content and metadata are held in Microsoft-managed Azure Storage dedicated to the case.
claims.quote: When you add content to a review set, the items and their metadata are copied to a Microsoft-managed Azure Storage location dedicated to the case.

claims.claim: Storage is provisioned per case and shared by the case's review sets.
claims.quote: Storage is provisioned per case. Multiple review sets within the same case share the underlying case storage, with logical separation so each review set's content remains independently queryable, taggable, and exportable.

claims.claim: Investigators can search review set content.
claims.quote: Review sets provide a static, known set of content that you can search, filter, tag, analyze, and predict relevancy using predictive coding models.

claims.claim: Investigators can filter review set content.
claims.quote: Review sets provide a static, known set of content that you can search, filter, tag, analyze, and predict relevancy using predictive coding models.

claims.where: What's changing: review set definition; Cost and licensing: reviewer time
claims.claim: Investigators can tag review set content.
claims.quote: Review sets provide a static, known set of content that you can search, filter, tag, analyze, and predict relevancy using predictive coding models.

claims.claim: Investigators can export review set content.
claims.quote: After the review set processing completes, select the Review sets tab in the case, then select the review set to start the process of filtering, reviewing, tagging, and exporting data in the review set.

claims.claim: When the tenant is configured with Customer Key, review set content at rest is encrypted with the customer-managed key.
claims.quote: If your tenant is configured with Customer Key, review set content at rest is encrypted with the customer-managed key.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: In data spillage scenarios, deleting the case is the only documented way to remove items in its review sets.
claims.quote: In data spillage scenarios, the only way to remove items in a review set is to delete the eDiscovery case. Other search and purge methods don't remove items from a review set.

claims.claim: Deleting a case deletes its searches.
claims.quote: When you delete a case, you also delete all components associated with the case, such as the list of communications, searches, review sets, and exports.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every hold policy in the case, including policies with status Off, must be deleted before the case can be deleted.
claims.quote: Before you can delete a case, you must delete all hold policies listed on the Hold policies tab of the case. This requirement includes deleting holds with a status of Off.

claims.claim: eDiscovery Managers can access review sets in cases they create and are members of.
claims.quote: eDiscovery Manager. Allows members to access review sets in eDiscovery cases they create and are members of.

claims.claim: eDiscovery Administrators can access review sets in all cases.
claims.quote: eDiscovery Administrator. Provides all the permissions of eDiscovery Manager, plus the ability to access review sets in all eDiscovery cases in the organization.

claims.claim: Reviewers have read-only access to review sets in cases where they are members.
claims.quote: Reviewer. Provides read-only access to review sets within eDiscovery cases where the user is a member. Reviewers can view and tag documents but cannot perform other case management tasks.
claims.fix: Replace 'a Reviewer has read-only access in cases where they are a member' with 'a Reviewer can view and tag documents in review sets in cases where they are a member, but cannot perform other case management tasks', as stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/security-ediscoverycase-post-reviewsets?view=graph-rest-1.0.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Manager can manage only cases they create.
claims.quote: However, eDiscovery Managers can only create and manage the cases they create.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Administrator can manage all cases.
claims.quote: Manage any eDiscovery case after they add themselves as a member of the case.
claims.fix: Replace 'an eDiscovery Administrator can access and manage all cases and configure eDiscovery settings' with 'an eDiscovery Administrator can access all cases, manage any case after adding themselves as a member, and configure eDiscovery settings', following https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-permissions.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Administrator can configure eDiscovery settings.
claims.quote: Additionally, an eDiscovery Administrator can: Configure eDiscovery solution settings.

claims.claim: Delegated use of the Graph operations in the table requires a supported Microsoft Purview eDiscovery role for the signed-in user.
claims.quote: For delegated access using work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Purview role through one of the following options:

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Review sets are created only by people holding eDiscovery roles, including when created through Graph.
claims.quote: Graph API app-only authentication: Graph API calls are made by the application itself, without a user context. The app authenticates using its own credentials
claims.fix: Replace the Autonomy & actions bullet with 'Review sets can be created from a search in the portal or through the Microsoft Graph API, whose create reviewSets operation supports application permissions.' In the risk rationale remove 'review sets are still created only by people holding eDiscovery roles, and'. The cited create reviewSets reference documents application permissions: https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/security-ediscoverycase-post-reviewsets?view=graph-rest-1.0.

claims.claim: This increase makes no change to who can reach review sets.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview eDiscovery review set limit increase 100 unchanged permissions access eDiscovery Manager Administrator'; read edisc-permissions, edisc and Graph create reviewSets. These state current permissions, not that this change leaves historical access unchanged.
claims.fix: Remove 'No change to who can reach review sets.' Keep the separately documented current role permissions.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope: Cases; rendered control table
claims.claim: Premium features are enabled by default for tenants with premium feature access.
claims.quote: Premium features are enabled by default for tenants with premium feature access.

claims.claim: Premium features can be turned off per case after creation.
claims.quote: Premium features are enabled by default for tenants with premium feature access. To turn off, toggle the setting after a case is created.

claims.claim: The tenant default for new cases is configured at Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Settings > eDiscovery > General > eDiscovery (Premium).
claims.quote: Select the eDiscovery solution card, then go to Settings > eDiscovery > General. Select or clear the toggle for eDiscovery (Premium).

claims.claim: Only eDiscovery Administrators can access the general default setting.
claims.quote: Only users assigned to the eDiscovery Administrators role can access this setting.

claims.claim: The general premium setting affects new cases only, not existing cases.
claims.quote: Enabling premium eDiscovery features only affects new cases and doesn't affect the license state of any existing cases.

claims.claim: eDiscovery Manager membership is assigned in Microsoft Purview portal at Settings > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Role groups. On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select eDiscovery Manager. Select Edit. On Manage eDiscovery Manager, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; rendered control table; Governance guidance

claims.fix: Add to controls[1].note: 'The cases dashboard documentation separately says access to premium features is not governed by the case settings toggle.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-cases-manage#cases-dashboard, which states 'Access to premium features isn't governed by the case settings toggle', alongside the existing case settings guidance that says to turn on the toggle to use premium features.
